ai_brain.title: Six adaptive learning modules running behind the core strategies
ai_brain.lead: Core strategies (SMC + Pivot Mean Reversion) are executed by a deterministic decision engine — quantitative math formulas + rule-based router. Every trade-by-trade decision is traceable in the SQL audit log. The AI advisor is a separate layer used only for research & web fetch (daily brief, market context); it NEVER gates execution.
ai_brain.disclaimer: The components below are part of the internal execution engine — they are not exposed as a public API. Deeper disclosure lives at /platform/risk-framework.
ai_brain.mod_bandit_title: Bandit Routing — Pick the best confluence
ai_brain.mod_bandit_desc: An A/B-testing-style system that automatically selects the confluence variant (Pure / + AO / + ADX / Full) best suited to the current market regime. Uses Thompson Sampling — the variant winning more often gets more signal allocation.
ai_brain.mod_kelly_desc: John Kelly's mathematical formula computes the optimal capital stake per trade from historical win rate + edge. BabahAlgo uses fractional Kelly (0.25-0.5 of full Kelly) so volatility spikes don't trigger overbetting.
ai_brain.mod_markov_desc: Take-profit slides automatically based on probabilistic state transitions: in a strong-momentum state TP gets pushed further out, in a reversal state TP gets pulled in. More accurate than a fixed R:R setting.
ai_brain.mod_winprob_desc: A machine-learning model scores the probability of profit per signal before execution. Signals below the confidence threshold are blocked — preventing marginal trades in less-than-ideal conditions.
ai_brain.mod_adaptive_title: Adaptive Exit — Learn from the equity curve
ai_brain.mod_adaptive_desc: Stop-loss adapts via deterministic rules: widening per ATR multiplier during high-vol regime, time-decay tighten when position holds past max threshold. Rules live in code, traceable in the execution log. Not an AI postmortem that "learns".
ai_brain.mod_isotonic_desc: AI confidence scores are calibrated against historical reality. When the AI says 70% confidence, the actual win rate should be ~70% (not overconfident). Important for traders who feed confidence into their sizing inputs.

platform_overview.hero_lead: BabahAlgo is a quantitative trading platform combining multi-strategy execution, AI-driven analysis, and institutional-grade risk management into a single, auditable pipeline.
platform_overview.pillars_lead: The platform is organized around three foundational disciplines. Each operates independently but reinforces the others.
platform_overview.pillar_strategy_desc: Three umbrella strategies live in production backend: SMC Scalper (Quasimodo family — Pure, AO, ADX, Full Confluence on M5-H1), SMC Swing (Quasimodo variants on H1-H4 for swing traders), and Pivot Mean Reversion (fade back to the daily pivot when overextended). Executed by a deterministic decision engine — rule-based strategy router picks the best confluence per regime, mathematical Kelly sizing tunes position size, adaptive stop engine refines TP/SL from the volatility profile. Every decision traceable in the SQL audit log.
platform_overview.pillar_technology_desc: A purpose-built execution pipeline anchored by Gemini 2.5 Flash for real-time analysis and confidence scoring, a ZeroMQ bridge delivering sub-2ms order routing, and MetaTrader 5 for broker connectivity. The entire stack runs on isolated VPS infrastructure behind Cloudflare Tunnel.
platform_overview.pillar_risk_desc: Capital preservation is not a feature — it is the architecture. Twelve independent risk layers operate simultaneously: dynamic lot sizing, catastrophic breakers, daily loss limits, spread guards, news blackout windows, session drawdown monitors, and more.
platform_overview.pipeline_lead: Every trade follows a deterministic pipeline with no manual intervention.
platform_overview.pipeline_step_1_desc: Real-time tick aggregation and candle construction
platform_overview.pipeline_step_2_desc: Gemini 2.5 Flash analysis, confidence scoring, bias
platform_overview.pipeline_step_4_desc: Risk validation: vol-target sizing, drawdown, correlation, spread, session
platform_overview.pipeline_step_6_desc: Order execution via broker liquidity pool
platform_overview.pipeline_step_7_desc: Fill confirmation, position tracking, equity reconciliation
platform_overview.instruments_lead: 14 instruments across four asset classes, selected for liquidity depth, spread efficiency, and strategy compatibility.
platform_overview.docs_methodology_desc: Complete description of strategy logic, entry/exit criteria, backtesting methodology, and walk-forward validation results.
platform_overview.docs_whitepaper_desc: Infrastructure architecture, security model, execution latency benchmarks, and formal risk framework specifications.

platform_technology.hero_title: AI engine, execution infrastructure, and monitoring.
platform_technology.hero_lead: Every component in the BabahAlgo technology stack is purpose-built for automated trading. There are no general-purpose frameworks, no shared hosting, and no third-party signal dependencies. The system owns the full pipeline from analysis to execution.
platform_technology.ai_card_p1: The AI advisor uses Google's Gemini 2.5 Flash model to perform real-time market analysis for each monitored instrument. Every 15 minutes, the system submits a structured prompt containing current OHLCV data, recent price action context, active position state, and recent trade history. The model returns a JSON-structured response with directional bias, confidence score, key support and resistance levels, timeframe-specific analysis, and risk commentary.
platform_technology.ai_card_p2: Confidence scoring operates on a 0-100 scale. Scores below 70 suppress new entries for the pair. Scores between 70-80 require full multi-timeframe technical confluence. Scores above 80 allow entry with reduced confluence requirements. A neutral bias reading pauses all new entries regardless of technical signals.
platform_technology.exec_zeromq_p1: Order routing between the strategy engine and MetaTrader 5 is handled by a custom ZeroMQ bridge. ZeroMQ is a high-performance asynchronous messaging library that provides socket-level communication without the overhead of HTTP or REST protocols. The bridge serializes trade commands (open, modify, close) into compact binary messages and transmits them to the MT5 expert advisor via TCP sockets on localhost.
platform_technology.exec_zeromq_p2: Measured end-to-end latency from signal generation to order submission is consistently below 2 milliseconds in production. This includes message serialization, socket transmission, deserialization, and MT5 order queue insertion. Actual fill latency depends on broker infrastructure and is typically 50-200ms additional.
platform_technology.exec_mt5_body: The MT5 expert advisor operates as a lightweight order executor. It receives commands from the ZeroMQ bridge, validates them against the broker's trading conditions (symbol availability, margin requirements, trading hours), and submits them to the broker's liquidity pool. Position management — including stop-loss modification, trailing stop ratcheting, and forced closure — is handled entirely through the bridge. The EA maintains no independent trading logic, ensuring the strategy engine is the single source of truth.
platform_technology.infra_zerotrust_body: All network access to the trading infrastructure is routed through Cloudflare Tunnel. There are no open ports, no public IP addresses exposed, and no direct SSH access from the internet. Administrative access requires Cloudflare Access authentication with hardware key verification. The tunnel provides DDoS protection, TLS termination, and access logging as a byproduct of its architecture.
platform_technology.infra_vps_body: The trading engine runs on a dedicated VPS with no shared tenancy. The server is provisioned with guaranteed CPU cores, dedicated RAM, and SSD storage to eliminate resource contention. The operating system is hardened with minimal attack surface — only the services required for trading operation are installed and running.
platform_technology.infra_db_body: All trading state — positions, signals, risk parameters, audit logs, account metrics — is persisted in PostgreSQL. The database provides ACID compliance, point-in-time recovery, and structured query capability for post-trade analysis. The entire application stack is containerized with Docker, enabling reproducible deployments, version-locked dependencies, and rapid rollback in the event of a deployment issue.
platform_technology.ops_health_body: Automated health checks run every 60 seconds, verifying connectivity to the broker, ZeroMQ bridge responsiveness, database availability, AI advisor reachability, and system resource utilization. Any check failure triggers an immediate alert to the operations team and initiates a pre-defined response protocol.
platform_technology.ops_killswitch_body: A hardware-level kill switch can halt all trading activity within seconds. When activated, the system closes all open positions at market, cancels all pending orders, and disables the strategy engine. The kill switch can be triggered manually through the admin dashboard, automatically by the catastrophic breaker risk layer, or remotely via an authenticated API endpoint.
platform_technology.ops_audit_body: Every action in the system is logged with a timestamp, actor identification, action type, and full payload. This includes trade signals generated, risk checks passed/failed, orders submitted, fills received, position modifications, and administrative actions. Logs are stored in PostgreSQL with a 90-day online retention and archived to cold storage for compliance purposes. All logs are available for query through the admin dashboard.

platform_risk.hero_title: Your capital is protected before, during, and after every trade.
platform_risk.hero_lead: We do more than place stop-losses. Every trade goes through four protection layers — from sizing the position safely, to managing exits dynamically, to braking the system when markets turn unfriendly. The same approach used by institutions like Bridgewater and AQR, restructured for individual accounts.
platform_risk.sec1_title: Position size adapts to market conditions
platform_risk.sec1_lead: Larger lots when markets are calm, smaller automatically when they're volatile. Before the broker receives the order, the system checks six things — volatility, signal strength, news calendar, and more. If any fails, the order is held back.
platform_risk.sec1_citation: Adapted from institutional standards: J.P. Morgan's RiskMetrics, AQR Capital, Bridgewater All-Weather, and Edward Thorp's Kelly framework.
platform_risk.sec1_rule1_desc: The system continuously tracks how unsettled price movements have been recently. When markets are quiet, your position is larger to capture opportunity; when markets are volatile, position size shrinks automatically so losses stay contained.
platform_risk.sec1_rule1_tech: Mechanism: EWMA volatility λ=0.94 daily / 0.97 monthly (RiskMetrics 1996 §5.1).
platform_risk.sec1_rule2_desc: Every trade order is rescaled based on current conditions — within sensible bounds that never balloon too large or shrink too small. The same approach institutions use to keep their annual returns stable.
platform_risk.sec1_rule2_tech: Mechanism: AQR "Risk Everywhere" vol-target scalar clamped 0.25× – 2.00× + Bridgewater All-Weather scaling pattern.
platform_risk.sec1_rule3_desc: Once a strategy has proven itself across a meaningful sample of trades, the system gradually trusts slightly larger positions. Until that track record exists, sizes stay conservative. Trust is earned, not assumed.
platform_risk.sec1_rule3_tech: Mechanism: fractional Kelly (Kelly 1956 + Thorp 1969), capped at 0.05 with a 53→100 trade sample-trust ramp.
platform_risk.sec1_rule4_desc: If you're long EURUSD and GBPUSD at the same time, you're effectively making the same dollar bet twice. The system recognizes this and rejects entries that pile risk on a single underlying factor.
platform_risk.sec1_rule4_tech: Mechanism: Pearson correlation matrix using timestamp-merge (Jane Street) — not naive positional alignment. Rejects entries that push correlation >0.7 with an open position.
platform_risk.sec1_rule5_desc: When the broker spread widens (typically during session transitions or right before news), new entries are rejected. The goal: you don't enter a market in execution conditions that put you at a disadvantage from the start.
platform_risk.sec1_rule5_tech: Per-instrument thresholds: 3 pip (EURUSD), 5 pip (XAUUSD), 8 pip (XNGUSD). Auto-skip pre-news + session transitions.
platform_risk.sec1_rule6_desc: Before NFP, FOMC, central bank decisions, or other major data, the system stops opening new positions on affected pairs. Event-driven volatility is the hardest environment for technicals — better to sit it out.
platform_risk.sec1_rule6_tech: Mechanism: high-impact event calendar (NFP, FOMC, ECB, BoJ, BoE, CPI, GDP) cached + 15min before to 5min after window blackout.
platform_risk.sec2_title: Adaptive exit, not a rigid stop-loss
platform_risk.sec2_lead: Many retail accounts lose not because the strategy is wrong, but because the exit isn't flexible. We chain eight automatic layers that manage every position from entry to closeout. Nothing is arbitrary — every rule has a reason that can be defended.
platform_risk.sec2_citation: Built from proven principles: ATR (Welles Wilder), R-multiple sizing (Van Tharp), 2×ATR stop convention (Jack Schwager), Cornix TP-ladder, and a rule-backed AI exit overlay.
platform_risk.sec2_citation_v2: Built from proven principles: ATR (Welles Wilder), R-multiple sizing (Van Tharp), 2×ATR stop convention (Jack Schwager), Cornix TP-ladder, and a rule-backed AI exit overlay.
platform_risk.sec2_layer1_desc: Every position has a stop-loss the moment it's opened, anchored to market structure (not a random distance). This stop can only be tightened — never widened in the losing direction. Your capital is protected from day one.
platform_risk.sec2_layer1_tech: Mechanism: SL anchored to order block (SMC), spring wick (Wyckoff), or ATR multiplier (momentum). Trailing + profit-lock layers own the tighten side.
platform_risk.sec2_layer2_desc: Instead of waiting for one large target that often slips away, we close 40% at the first level, 35% at the second, and let 25% run. This is consistently more reliable than the all-or-nothing exit common in retail.
platform_risk.sec2_layer2_tech: Mechanism: Cornix-style 3-rung TP ladder at 1R / 2R / 3R, JSONB-persistent state. Transactional ladder mutation prevents duplicate partial-close.
platform_risk.sec2_layer25_name: Lock small wins before they vanish
platform_risk.sec2_layer25_desc: Ever watch a position turn profit, then drift back to zero before hitting target? The system recognizes that pattern and quietly secures part of the gain after the move toward you stalls — so a near-win doesn't become a loss.
platform_risk.sec2_layer25_tech: Mechanism: trigger at 1×ATR (Wilder noise floor / AQR) or 0.3R floor (Tharp R-multiple) after 30min stagnation; vol-regime adaptive close ratio 20/30/45% (half-Kelly per Thorp).
platform_risk.sec2_layer26_name: Stop-loss widens when markets get wild
platform_risk.sec2_layer26_desc: When a surprise news spike hits, the original SL often gets clipped not because the setup was wrong, but because market noise simply expanded. The system recognizes this and widens the SL to a sensible distance for the new conditions — with a strict ceiling so the risk you authorized doesn't quietly double.
platform_risk.sec2_layer26_tech: Mechanism: fires when current ATR ≥ 1.5× implied entry ATR, target SL = 2× new ATR (Wilder/Schwager 2×ATR convention), hard cap 2× original risk_distance.
platform_risk.sec2_layer3_name: Trailing stop that follows the trend
platform_risk.sec2_layer3_desc: Once the first target is hit, the system starts trailing the stop along the trend. It only moves in your favor — never backward. The result: long trends capture most of the move; sudden reversals book profit at a much better level.
platform_risk.sec2_layer3_tech: Mechanism: monotonic tighter-only trailing, activates from TP1 hit. ATR multiplier adapts to vol regime: low-vol 1.5×, mid 2.5×, high 4.0× (AQR regime scaling).
platform_risk.sec2_layer4_desc: Every trade opens with an assumption about market structure. The moment that structure flips against you, the system closes immediately — without waiting for the SL. Better a small loss now than a large loss "hoping" later.
platform_risk.sec2_layer4_tech: Mechanism: BoS-flip detection (long force-closes on lower-low in an uptrend); Wyckoff Spring invalidation on price re-entry into the trading range.
platform_risk.sec2_layer5_desc: Scalping setups that haven't profited within 4 hours, or swings within 24, usually have a weakened thesis. The system auto-closes at the time cap and re-enters when a fresh valid signal appears. Capital isn't trapped in stale positions.
platform_risk.sec2_layer5_tech: Mechanism: hard cap 4h (scalp) / 24h (swing). Pre-news 30min: affected positions tightened to breakeven (not force-closed).
platform_risk.sec2_layer6_name: AI overseer as the final layer
platform_risk.sec2_layer6_desc: After five deterministic layers, an AI advisor (Claude Opus) reviews the exit context. It has four hard rules it can't break: never override the SL, never hold through a news blackout, never keep an invalidated position, never trade when the AI budget is spent. AI here is a second opinion — not the sole decision maker.
platform_risk.sec2_layer6_tech: Mechanism: Claude Opus with 4 explicit veto rules; verdicts logged to ai.advice_log. AI cannot override layers 1-5.
platform_risk.sec3_title: Auto-brake when the day isn't going well
platform_risk.sec3_lead: If the system has crossed a daily loss threshold or hit a losing streak, the kill-switch activates. But not as a crude 12-hour stop — we use a tiered approach that mirrors major exchanges (NYSE, Jane Street): a brief cool-down, then a probation period, then back to normal only if performance recovers.
platform_risk.sec3_citation: The circuit-breaker pattern is inspired by NYSE LULD, Jane Street, and prop-firm standards (FTMO, MyForexFunds). Adapted to run automatically for individual accounts.
platform_risk.sec3_trigger1_desc: If today's combined loss reaches the configured limit, all positions close and no new trades are allowed until tomorrow. One bad day shouldn't consume a month's risk budget.
platform_risk.sec3_trigger1_tech: Trigger DAILY_LOSS: realized + unrealized > 2-3% SoD equity. Auto-resolves at the next 00:00 UTC midnight.
platform_risk.sec3_trigger2_desc: After five consecutive losses, the system pauses briefly. It's not necessarily that the strategy failed — sometimes the market is simply in a phase where the strategy doesn't work. Better to step back and reassess than "try to make it back" and dig deeper.
platform_risk.sec3_trigger2_tech: Trigger LOSS_STREAK (default 5 consecutive). Adaptive: low-impact gets fast 1h cooling, escalates to 12h if probation fails. VIP/DEDICATED tier: admin-only review.
platform_risk.sec3_trigger3_desc: When equity drops beyond a sane intraday threshold, the system stops. To resume, equity must recover to a defined level — preventing a hasty re-entry before conditions improve.
platform_risk.sec3_trigger3_tech: Trigger EQUITY_DRAWDOWN: intraday drawdown >6% of Start-of-Day equity (anchored to SoD, not all-time peak). Retail self-ack: 24h cooling + ≥50% equity recovery.
platform_risk.sec3_state1_desc: If the kill-switch trigger is mild (sudden volatility, news spike), the system only stops for an hour. There's no point locking down for 12 hours when the "wild" market was a passing event, not a systemic strategy issue.
platform_risk.sec3_state1_tech: FAST 1h Cooling: for single-trigger low-impact events. Auto-release into PROBATION after 1 hour.
platform_risk.sec3_state2_desc: After cooldown, the system enters cautious mode: position size halved, signal confirmation thresholds raised, and only one simultaneous position per strategy. The goal: ease back into the market, not jump straight to full size.
platform_risk.sec3_state2_tech: PROBATION 4h: risk_pct halved 1% → 0.5%, min_confluence + 10, max_positions clamped to 1 per engine. 4-hour window.
platform_risk.sec3_state3_desc: During probation, the system evaluates every 5 minutes. Three winners in a row → back to normal mode. A single loss → escalated to a stricter 12-hour lockout. Performance decides, not a rigid timer.
platform_risk.sec3_state3_tech: Outcome-based validator + AI postmortem (Claude Opus, min_confidence 80) as primary release path. 5min grace prevents verdict flapping.
platform_risk.sec4_title: Every decision is logged and can't be edited
platform_risk.sec4_lead: Your trades run on automated systems — naturally you'll want to know what actually happened. Every order, policy decision, and price change is permanently recorded. If you need an independent audit, the trail is there. The same standard regulated banks operate on.
platform_risk.sec4_citation: Audit mechanisms follow the pattern Stripe uses for API records, plus the encryption-at-rest standard from HashiCorp Vault.
platform_risk.sec4_item1_desc: Every order open, close, SL/TP modification, and AI decision is written to a log that cannot be edited or deleted — not even by us as operators. If a dispute arises, the full digital trail is available for you to audit.
platform_risk.sec4_item1_tech: Mechanism: SHA-256 hash chain in PostgreSQL (audit.audit_chain), append-only via no-update / no-delete triggers. Tamper detection verify_chain() <5ms.
platform_risk.sec4_item2_name: Your data isolated from other customers
platform_risk.sec4_item2_desc: Each customer account has strict data separation enforced at the database level. Even if our application code had a bug, your trades are not visible to other customers — the isolation lives in PostgreSQL itself, not just in the app layer.
platform_risk.sec4_item2_tech: Mechanism: ContextVar tenant_context_var via with_tenant_context CM + PostgreSQL Row-Level Security (RLS) policies enforced at the query layer. ADR-001 multi-tenant from day one.
platform_risk.sec4_item3_name: Passwords & API keys protected by encryption
platform_risk.sec4_item3_desc: No plaintext passwords or tokens are stored on our servers. Everything is hashed or encrypted in a dedicated secret vault (HashiCorp Vault). Even we can't read customer passwords.
platform_risk.sec4_item3_tech: Mechanism: HashiCorp Vault 8201 for all secrets at rest. Tenant API tokens are SHA-256 hashed; plaintext returned ONCE at rotate. Vault auto-unseal via mount key envelope.
platform_risk.sec4_item4_desc: Every AI advisor invocation is recomputed against our own pricing tables — we don't simply pass through provider invoices. You can request a per-trade cost breakdown if you want. No surprise charges.
platform_risk.sec4_item4_tech: Mechanism: provider cost_usd is ignored. Cost recomputed from token counts × model price table with ROUND_HALF_UP 6dp (FinOps CUR pattern).

platform_execution.hero_lead: Execution quality determines whether a valid signal becomes a profitable trade. The BabahAlgo execution infrastructure is engineered for minimal latency, maximum reliability, and complete auditability at every stage of the order lifecycle.
platform_execution.latency_card_p1: The ZeroMQ bridge is the critical link between the strategy engine (running in Docker on Linux) and MetaTrader 5 (running on Windows). Communication occurs over TCP sockets on localhost, eliminating network latency entirely. Messages are serialized using a compact binary protocol that encodes trade commands (OPEN, MODIFY, CLOSE) with full parameters (symbol, direction, lot size, stop-loss, take-profit) in under 100 bytes per message.
platform_execution.latency_card_p2: The bridge operates in a request-reply pattern: the strategy engine sends a command and blocks until the MT5 EA confirms receipt and processing. This synchronous pattern ensures order integrity — no command is lost or duplicated. Measured round-trip latency in production consistently falls below 2 milliseconds.
platform_execution.broker_p1: MetaTrader 5 serves as the broker connectivity layer. The MT5 expert advisor is a stateless order executor — it receives commands from the ZeroMQ bridge, validates them against the broker's trading conditions, and submits them to the liquidity pool. The EA performs pre-submission checks including symbol availability, minimum lot size compliance, margin sufficiency, and trading hours validation.
platform_execution.broker_p2: Order types supported include market orders (immediate execution), pending limit orders, and stop orders. All orders include attached stop-loss and take-profit levels set at the time of submission. Position modifications (stop adjustment, trailing stop ratchet) are handled as separate MODIFY commands through the bridge.
platform_execution.broker_p3: Fill confirmations are returned to the strategy engine through the same ZeroMQ channel, including the actual fill price, slippage (if any), and the broker-assigned ticket number. This data is logged to PostgreSQL for reconciliation and slippage analysis.
platform_execution.vps_hardware_body: The trading engine runs on a dedicated VPS with guaranteed resources: no shared CPU cores, no memory overcommitment, and NVMe SSD storage for database I/O. The server is located in a data center with redundant power, cooling, and network connectivity. Physical proximity to major broker servers minimizes network latency for the final leg of order transmission.
platform_execution.vps_security_body: All external access is routed through Cloudflare Tunnel. The VPS has no publicly exposed ports. Administrative access requires Cloudflare Access authentication. Internal communication between Docker containers occurs on an isolated bridge network. The MT5 terminal communicates with the broker through its native encrypted protocol, and with the strategy engine exclusively through the localhost ZeroMQ socket.
platform_execution.ops_health_body: A dedicated monitoring service polls all critical components every 60 seconds: ZeroMQ bridge connectivity, MT5 terminal status, broker connection state, PostgreSQL availability, and system resource utilization (CPU, memory, disk). Each check has a defined healthy/degraded/critical threshold. Degraded status triggers a warning notification. Critical status triggers the automated response protocol.
platform_execution.ops_response_intro: When a critical health check failure is detected, the system follows a deterministic response sequence:
platform_execution.ops_response_step_1: Immediately pause all new trade signals
platform_execution.ops_response_step_3: If recovery fails within 30 seconds, close all open positions at market
platform_execution.ops_response_step_4: Disable the strategy engine and enter safe mode
platform_execution.ops_response_step_5: Send critical alert to the operations team with full diagnostic payload
platform_execution.ops_response_step_6: Log the entire incident timeline for post-mortem analysis
platform_execution.ops_uptime_body: The system targets 99.9% uptime during market hours (Sunday 17:00 ET to Friday 17:00 ET). Scheduled maintenance windows are limited to weekends when markets are closed. Unscheduled downtime triggers the automated response protocol described above, ensuring that positions are never left unmanaged during an outage.

platform_instruments.hero_lead: Each instrument is selected based on liquidity depth, spread efficiency, strategy compatibility, and historical performance characteristics. The platform does not trade thinly-traded or exotic instruments.
platform_instruments.desc_forex: Seven major and minor currency pairs selected for deep liquidity, tight spreads, and strong trending characteristics. These pairs form the core of the SMC Scalper, SMC Swing, and Pivot Mean Reversion strategies.
platform_instruments.desc_metals: Gold and silver provide portfolio diversification and safe-haven exposure. These instruments respond to macro risk sentiment, inflation expectations, and central bank policy, offering uncorrelated return streams.
platform_instruments.desc_energy: WTI Crude, Brent Crude, and Natural Gas are monitored using the same liquidity and volatility filters as forex pairs, applying SMC Scalper and SMC Swing strategies optimized for the trending characteristics of energy commodities.
platform_instruments.desc_crypto: Bitcoin and Ethereum are monitored for high-conviction momentum setups. Due to their higher volatility, position sizes are reduced and spread guard thresholds are elevated.
platform_instruments.criteria_intro: Instruments are evaluated quarterly against four criteria before inclusion or removal from the active universe:
platform_instruments.criteria_liquidity_body: Average daily volume must exceed minimum thresholds to ensure consistent fill quality and manageable slippage.
platform_instruments.criteria_spread_body: Average spread during active trading hours must remain below the strategy-specific threshold to maintain positive expected value after transaction costs.
platform_instruments.criteria_compatibility_body: The instrument must demonstrate technical characteristics (trending behavior, mean-reversion, or event-driven patterns) compatible with at least one active strategy.
platform_instruments.criteria_performance_body: Backtested and walk-forward results for the instrument must meet minimum performance thresholds (win rate, risk-reward ratio, drawdown limits) before live deployment.

platform_strategies.hero_lead: Three production-grade strategies live in the backend, each operating on strict multi-timeframe confluence. Every strategy is backtested over at least 24 months of historical data and validated through walk-forward analysis before deployment, with an adaptive math engine (rule-based strategy router, mathematical Kelly sizing, adaptive stop rule) running in the background — fully deterministic.
platform_strategies.hero_disclaimer: Win-rate values below are from in-house backtest (24-month walk-forward, Q1 2024–Q4 2025). Live track record publishes after Q3 2026 — past performance does not guarantee future results.
platform_strategies.smc_desc: Smart Money Concepts applied to intraday timeframes. Identifies institutional order flow through order blocks, fair value gaps, breaker blocks, and the Quasimodo pattern. Four confluence layers (Pure, AO, ADX, Full) are auto-routed by a rule-based bandit router (statistical Thompson Sampling) per market regime — each has a distinct volatility + trend signature. Fits ranging market conditions (ADX < 20) on major pairs + Gold. Moderate win rate with low R:R but high frequency — smooth equity curve, ideal for compounding capital growth.

platform_strategy_detail.smc_abstract_1: Smart Money Concepts (SMC) is a structural approach to price action analysis that seeks to identify the footprints left by institutional participants -- banks, hedge funds, and proprietary trading desks -- as they accumulate and distribute positions. Unlike retail-oriented indicator strategies, SMC focuses on the mechanics of liquidity: where it rests, how it is engineered, and when it is harvested. The BabahAlgo SMC Intraday strategy automates this process through algorithmic detection of order blocks, fair value gaps, breaker blocks, and liquidity sweeps across multiple timeframes.
platform_strategy_detail.smc_abstract_2: The strategy operates primarily on the M5 to H1 range, using H4 for directional bias and H1 for structural context. Entry signals are generated when M15 structure aligns with the higher-timeframe narrative, with M5 providing precision timing. Every signal must pass through the full institutional risk framework before execution. The system is designed for high-frequency intraday operation, targeting 3-8 trades per day across the seven major forex pairs, with a strict maximum hold duration of 4 hours.
platform_strategy_detail.smc_mechanism_1: H4 bias determination: Identify premium/discount zones relative to the current dealing range. Determine whether price is in an institutional accumulation or distribution phase based on swing structure and volume profile.
platform_strategy_detail.smc_mechanism_2: H1 structural mapping: Mark active order blocks (last bearish candle before a bullish impulse, or vice versa), fair value gaps (three-candle imbalances), and breaker blocks (failed order blocks that become support/resistance). Identify key liquidity pools above swing highs and below swing lows.
platform_strategy_detail.smc_mechanism_3: M15 confluence check: Wait for a change of character (CHoCH) or break of structure (BOS) that aligns with the H4 bias. Confirm that the move originates from a valid H1 point of interest (order block, FVG, or breaker).
platform_strategy_detail.smc_mechanism_4: M5 entry trigger: Refine entry using M5 order flow. Look for a mitigation of an M5 order block within the M15 zone, combined with a displacement candle (strong momentum candle with body > 70% of range). Enter at the close of the displacement candle or on a retest of the M5 order block.
platform_strategy_detail.smc_mechanism_5: Stop placement: Place the protective stop below the M15 swing low (for longs) or above the M15 swing high (for shorts), ensuring it sits beyond the institutional reference point. Typical stop distance is 15-25 pips on major pairs.
platform_strategy_detail.smc_mechanism_6: Target calculation: Primary target at the nearest H1 liquidity pool or opposing order block. Secondary target at the H4 premium/discount boundary. Use a trailing mechanism that ratchets to breakeven after 1R profit.

platform_strategy_detail.wyckoff_abstract_1: The Wyckoff method, developed by Richard D. Wyckoff in the early 20th century, remains one of the most rigorous frameworks for understanding market structure. It posits that markets move through repeating phases of accumulation (institutional buying), markup (trending), distribution (institutional selling), and markdown (declining). The BabahAlgo Wyckoff strategy automates the identification of these phases through algorithmic volume-price analysis, spring/upthrust detection, and phase transition confirmation.
platform_strategy_detail.wyckoff_abstract_2: This strategy operates on the M15 to H4 range, giving it a slightly longer holding period than the SMC Intraday approach. It is particularly effective in ranging markets where accumulation and distribution phases are clearly delineated. The system monitors volume divergences, effort-versus-result relationships, and the sequential appearance of Wyckoff events (preliminary support, selling climax, automatic rally, secondary test, spring) to build a probabilistic model of phase progression. Trades are only initiated when the phase model reaches high confidence and the entry aligns with a valid Wyckoff event.
platform_strategy_detail.wyckoff_mechanism_1: Phase identification: Continuously classify the current market phase (accumulation, markup, distribution, markdown) using a composite of price range analysis, volume profile, and swing point sequencing. Update phase confidence scores on every H1 close.
platform_strategy_detail.wyckoff_mechanism_2: Event detection: Monitor for Wyckoff events within the identified phase. In accumulation: preliminary support (PS), selling climax (SC), automatic rally (AR), secondary test (ST), and spring. In distribution: preliminary supply (PSY), buying climax (BC), automatic reaction (AR), secondary test (ST), and upthrust (UT).
platform_strategy_detail.wyckoff_mechanism_3: Volume-price divergence: Analyze effort versus result on each swing. A declining volume on a test of support in accumulation, or declining volume on a test of resistance in distribution, confirms institutional intent.
platform_strategy_detail.wyckoff_mechanism_4: Spring/upthrust entry: The primary entry signal is the spring (a brief penetration below the trading range low that is immediately reversed) in accumulation, or the upthrust (a brief penetration above the range high) in distribution. Enter on the reversal candle close with stop beyond the spring/upthrust wick.
platform_strategy_detail.wyckoff_mechanism_5: Sign of strength confirmation: After entry, monitor for a sign of strength (SOS) -- a strong impulsive move away from the trading range on increasing volume -- to confirm phase transition. If SOS does not appear within the expected window, tighten stops to breakeven.
platform_strategy_detail.wyckoff_mechanism_6: Target projection: Project targets using the point-and-figure count method applied to the trading range width. Primary target equals the range width added to the breakout point. Secondary target at 1.618x the range width.

platform_strategy_detail.astronacci_abstract_1: The Astronacci strategy represents a proprietary synthesis of harmonic price geometry and cyclical timing analysis. At its core, the system identifies zones where multiple Fibonacci retracement and extension levels converge -- creating "clusters" of mathematical significance that historically correspond to high-probability reversal or continuation points. These geometric confluences are then cross-referenced with planetary cycle timing windows to filter entries to periods of heightened market sensitivity.
platform_strategy_detail.astronacci_abstract_2: Operating primarily on the H1 to H4 range, this strategy is designed for swing-style entries with moderate holding periods. The system continuously maps Fibonacci levels from multiple swing points across timeframes, scoring each zone by the density of overlapping levels. When a high-density zone coincides with a cyclical timing window, the system flags a potential setup. Entry is confirmed only when price action within the zone demonstrates a reversal pattern consistent with the expected direction. This multi-layer approach reduces false signals significantly compared to single-timeframe Fibonacci strategies.
platform_strategy_detail.astronacci_mechanism_1: Multi-swing Fibonacci mapping: Calculate Fibonacci retracement (23.6%, 38.2%, 50%, 61.8%, 78.6%) and extension (127.2%, 161.8%, 200%) levels from every significant swing point on H4 and H1 timeframes. A significant swing is defined as a pivot that exceeds the average true range of the surrounding 20 candles.
platform_strategy_detail.astronacci_mechanism_2: Confluence zone scoring: Identify price levels where three or more Fibonacci levels from different swing points converge within a tolerance of 0.1% of price. Score each zone by the number of overlapping levels and the quality of the source swings. Zones scoring 5+ are classified as high-priority.
platform_strategy_detail.astronacci_mechanism_3: Cyclical timing alignment: Cross-reference high-priority zones with planetary cycle timing windows derived from lunar, solar, and planetary aspect calculations. Setups that fall within active timing windows receive elevated priority.
platform_strategy_detail.astronacci_mechanism_4: Price action confirmation: Within a valid zone during an active window, monitor for reversal candlestick patterns on M15: engulfing patterns, pin bars (wicks > 2x body), or inside bar breakouts. The confirmation candle must close within or beyond the confluence zone.
platform_strategy_detail.astronacci_mechanism_5: Entry and stop: Enter at the close of the confirmation candle. Place stop beyond the far edge of the confluence zone plus a buffer of 0.5x ATR(14). This ensures the stop respects the geometric boundary that defines the setup.
platform_strategy_detail.astronacci_mechanism_6: Harmonic target projection: Primary target at the next high-priority confluence zone in the direction of the trade. Secondary target at the 161.8% Fibonacci extension of the entry swing. Trail stops using a 2x ATR ratchet after 1R profit.

platform_strategy_detail.ai-momentum_abstract_1: The AI Momentum strategy represents the convergence of traditional momentum analysis with modern large language model capabilities. At its foundation, the system uses Gemini 2.5 Flash to perform real-time analysis of market structure, news sentiment, and cross-pair correlation for each monitored instrument. The AI generates a structured assessment including directional bias, confidence score (0-100), key support/resistance levels, and a risk commentary. This AI layer acts as the first filter -- only setups where the AI confidence exceeds the strategy threshold proceed to the technical momentum engine.
platform_strategy_detail.ai-momentum_abstract_2: The technical momentum engine operates on M15 to H1, combining rate-of-change analysis, volume-weighted momentum scoring, and ADX trend strength filtering to classify the current momentum regime (strong trend, weak trend, ranging, or transitioning). Trades are initiated only when the AI directional bias aligns with a strong or accelerating momentum regime, creating a dual-confirmation system that reduces false signals in choppy or transitioning markets. The result is a strategy that captures genuine momentum moves while avoiding the whipsaws that plague traditional momentum approaches.
platform_strategy_detail.ai-momentum_mechanism_1: AI analysis cycle: Every 15 minutes, submit current market state (OHLCV data, recent price action, open positions, recent trade history) to Gemini 2.5 Flash with a structured prompt. Receive a JSON response containing: directional bias (LONG/SHORT/NEUTRAL), confidence score (0-100), key levels, timeframe assessment, and risk notes.
platform_strategy_detail.ai-momentum_mechanism_2: Confidence filtering: Only proceed with setups where AI confidence >= 70. Setups with confidence 70-80 require full technical confluence. Setups with confidence > 80 may proceed with reduced confluence requirements. Neutral bias signals pause new entries for the pair.
platform_strategy_detail.ai-momentum_mechanism_3: Momentum regime classification: Calculate 14-period and 28-period rate of change on H1. Compute volume-weighted momentum score using tick volume as a proxy. Read ADX(14) to assess trend strength. Classify regime: Strong Trend (ADX > 25, ROC aligned), Weak Trend (ADX 20-25), Ranging (ADX < 20), Transitioning (ADX crossing 20-25 zone).
platform_strategy_detail.ai-momentum_mechanism_4: Entry signal: Generate an entry signal when AI bias is LONG or SHORT, confidence >= threshold, and the momentum regime is classified as Strong Trend or Transitioning-to-Strong. Enter on the close of an M15 candle that confirms the direction with a body-to-range ratio > 60%.
platform_strategy_detail.ai-momentum_mechanism_5: Dynamic position sizing: Adjust lot size based on AI confidence level and current account equity. Higher confidence scores allow marginally larger position sizes within the risk framework limits. All sizing remains subject to the institutional risk filter (vol-target + Kelly cap + correlation guard).
platform_strategy_detail.ai-momentum_mechanism_6: Adaptive exit: Primary exit at the AI-identified key level in the profit direction. Trailing stop activates after 1R using an ATR-based ratchet. If AI confidence drops below 50 on a subsequent cycle while the position is open, tighten stops to breakeven regardless of current P&L.

platform_strategy_detail.oil-gas_abstract_1: The Oil & Gas Macro strategy is a specialist approach designed exclusively for energy markets: USOIL (WTI Crude), UKOIL (Brent Crude), and XNGUSD (Natural Gas). Energy markets behave differently from forex pairs -- they are driven by supply-demand fundamentals (inventory data, OPEC decisions, seasonal demand cycles), geopolitical risk events, and weather patterns. A pure technical approach misses these dominant drivers. This strategy integrates fundamental data cycles with technical confluence to time entries around high-impact events.
platform_strategy_detail.oil-gas_abstract_2: The system maintains a rolling fundamental model that tracks EIA inventory data release cycles, OPEC meeting schedules, seasonal demand patterns (winter heating, summer driving), and geopolitical risk scoring for key producing regions. When the fundamental model identifies a directional bias (e.g., inventory drawdown plus seasonal demand increase), the technical engine activates to find optimal entry points using supply/demand zone analysis on H1-H4 timeframes. This dual approach captures moves driven by fundamental catalysts while maintaining disciplined technical entries and risk management.
platform_strategy_detail.oil-gas_mechanism_1: Fundamental calendar tracking: Maintain a real-time calendar of EIA weekly inventory reports (Wednesday 10:30 ET), API inventory estimates (Tuesday 16:30 ET), OPEC meeting dates, and seasonal transition windows. Pre-position bias expectations before each data release based on market consensus and historical seasonal patterns.
platform_strategy_detail.oil-gas_mechanism_2: Geopolitical risk scoring: Monitor a composite risk score for energy-producing regions (Middle East, Russia, US shale). Elevated risk scores increase directional bias for long positions. The score is derived from news sentiment analysis processed through the AI advisor.
platform_strategy_detail.oil-gas_mechanism_3: Supply-demand zone mapping on H4: Identify institutional supply and demand zones on H4 using volume-profile analysis. Mark zones where price spent minimal time (indicating rapid institutional order absorption). These zones serve as the primary areas of interest for entries.
platform_strategy_detail.oil-gas_mechanism_4: H1 structural confirmation: Within an H4 supply/demand zone, wait for H1 to form a reversal structure -- a break of structure or change of character that aligns with the fundamental bias. This confirms that the technical picture supports the fundamental expectation.
platform_strategy_detail.oil-gas_mechanism_5: Entry on M15 with fundamental alignment: Enter on an M15 confirmation candle within the H1 reversal structure, but only during the 2-hour window surrounding a scheduled data release (for event-driven trades) or when the seasonal model is active (for trend-following trades).
platform_strategy_detail.oil-gas_mechanism_6: Volatility-adjusted stops: Energy markets exhibit higher volatility than forex. Stops are calculated using 2.5x ATR(14) on the entry timeframe, with a minimum of 50 pips for crude oil and 30 pips for natural gas. Targets use a 1:2 minimum risk-reward ratio.
platform_strategy_detail.oil-gas_confluence_1_role: Supply-demand zone identification and fundamental alignment
platform_strategy_detail.oil-gas_confluence_4_role: Precision entry and volatility-adjusted stop placement
platform_strategy_detail.smc-swing_abstract_1: The SMC Swing strategy extends the Smart Money Concepts framework to higher timeframes, targeting multi-day moves that originate from weekly and daily institutional order flow. While the SMC Intraday strategy captures quick liquidity grabs on lower timeframes, SMC Swing operates in the H4 to D1 range, seeking positions that align with the broader institutional dealing range. The result is a lower-frequency, higher-conviction strategy with larger targets and proportionally wider stops.
platform_strategy_detail.smc-swing_abstract_2: This strategy is designed for traders and institutional API clients that prioritize capital efficiency over trade frequency. By operating on higher timeframes, SMC Swing naturally filters out the noise and false signals that affect intraday approaches. The system identifies weekly premium and discount zones, maps daily order blocks and liquidity pools, and enters on H4 structural confirmations. Typical holding periods range from 8 to 48 hours, with the maximum capped at the system-wide 4-hour limit for risk management. Positions that require longer holds are structured as re-entries at the next valid setup rather than extended single holds.
platform_strategy_detail.smc-swing_mechanism_1: Weekly dealing range: On every weekly close, calculate the weekly premium (upper 50%) and discount (lower 50%) zones. Determine whether the prior week closed in premium or discount relative to the 20-week range. This establishes the macro directional bias -- seek longs in discount, shorts in premium.
platform_strategy_detail.smc-swing_mechanism_2: Daily order block identification: Map daily order blocks as the last opposing candle before an impulsive daily move. Qualify blocks by checking that the subsequent impulse was at least 2x the daily ATR. Mark the open and close of the order block candle as the zone of interest.
platform_strategy_detail.smc-swing_mechanism_3: Daily liquidity pool mapping: Identify clusters of equal highs and equal lows on the daily chart. These represent resting liquidity (stop orders) that institutional participants are likely to target. The system tracks these pools as potential targets and potential entry triggers (after a sweep).
platform_strategy_detail.smc-swing_mechanism_4: H4 structural entry: Wait for price to enter a daily order block or to sweep a daily liquidity pool. Then monitor H4 for a change of character (CHoCH) that indicates the institutional move has begun. Enter on the first H4 candle that closes beyond the CHoCH level.
platform_strategy_detail.smc-swing_mechanism_5: Stop and target: Place stop beyond the daily order block boundary (the far edge of the qualifying candle). This is typically 40-80 pips on major pairs. Primary target at the nearest daily liquidity pool in the profit direction. Secondary target at the opposing weekly zone boundary.
platform_strategy_detail.smc-swing_mechanism_6: Re-entry protocol: If the trade reaches its maximum hold duration before target, close the position. If the daily structure remains valid, re-enter on the next H4 CHoCH within the same daily zone. This allows the strategy to capture multi-day moves through a series of intraday positions rather than a single extended hold.
platform_strategy_detail.smc-swing_confluence_1_role: Dealing range, order block, and liquidity pool mapping
platform_strategy_detail.pivot-mean-reversion_subtitle: Fade back to the daily pivot when price overextends
platform_strategy_detail.pivot-mean-reversion_abstract_1: Pivot Mean Reversion is an institutional scalping strategy that exploits the market's central tendency. Each day, the forex market forms a daily pivot point (PP) — the average of yesterday's high-low-close that acts as a price magnet. When the market isn't strongly trending (ranging conditions or a weak-trend pullback), price tends to revert to the pivot after excursions to R1/R2 (resistance) or S1/S2 (support). BabahAlgo Pivot Mean Reversion automates excursion detection and entry timing for disciplined fades back to the pivot.
platform_strategy_detail.pivot-mean-reversion_abstract_2: The strategy operates on M5-M15 timeframes with a trend-regime filter on H1. The system is only active when the regime detector identifies a ranging market (ADX < 20 or ATR percentile rank < 40). Win rate is moderate (~57%) with R:R 1:1.3 — the equity curve is smooth thanks to frequent, small, consistent trades. Capital protection comes from tight stops (15-20 pips beyond swing extrema) and a session-aware kill-switch (the system stands down during the London/NY overlap). The adaptive math engine (mathematical Kelly sizing + adaptive stop rule) tunes position size and trailing logic from the volatility profile + the trader's historical equity curve — all rule-based, deterministic, traceable.
platform_strategy_detail.pivot-mean-reversion_mechanism_1: Daily pivot calculation: Daily Pivot (PP) = (yesterday's High + Low + Close) / 3. Resistance R1 = 2×PP − Low, R2 = PP + (High − Low). Support S1 = 2×PP − High, S2 = PP − (High − Low). Calculation is automatic at the UTC session rollover and pinned as static levels for 24 hours.
platform_strategy_detail.pivot-mean-reversion_mechanism_2: H1 regime filter: The system checks ADX(14) and ATR percentile rank on H1. The strategy is only active when ADX < 20 (ranging) AND ATR percentile rank < 40 (normal-to-low volatility). When the market trends strongly (ADX > 25), the strategy is auto-paused to avoid fading against trend.
platform_strategy_detail.pivot-mean-reversion_mechanism_3: M15 overextension detection: Monitor price touching or piercing R1/R2 or S1/S2. Confirm with RSI(7) in overbought (> 75) for R1/R2 or oversold (< 25) for S1/S2. Identify M15 reversal candle patterns (pin bar, engulfing, inside-bar breakout reversal) at the level touch.
platform_strategy_detail.pivot-mean-reversion_mechanism_4: M5 entry trigger: After an M15 reversal pattern appears, await M5 confirmation — a candle closing back below R1 (short) or back above S1 (long). Entry on the next candle's open. No entry if a high-impact news event lies within the next 30 minutes (news guard).
platform_strategy_detail.pivot-mean-reversion_mechanism_5: Stop placement: Stop is placed 15-20 pips beyond the swing high (short) or swing low (long) formed in the reversal pattern. For higher-ATR pairs (Gold XAUUSD, GBP crosses), stops can scale to 25-30 pips. Position size is computed via fractional Kelly so risk per trade stays consistent (0.25-0.5 Kelly, never full Kelly).
platform_strategy_detail.pivot-mean-reversion_mechanism_6: Target and exit protocol: Primary target at the daily PP (daily pivot). Secondary target at the opposing pivot level (if short from R1, secondary at S1). Trailing stop activates after 1R profit. Maximum hold is 4 hours — if PP isn't hit within 4 hours, close at market (time stop). AI adaptive exit can override when continuation momentum is detected.

legal_privacy_body.s1_communication_text: We retain records of your communications with us, including support requests, feedback, and correspondence via email, WhatsApp, or our contact form.

legal_privacy_body.s2_li3: To deliver trading signals, performance reports, and account notifications

legal_privacy_body.s2_li5: To comply with legal obligations and regulatory requirements

legal_privacy_body.s4_legal_text: We may disclose your information when required by law, regulation, legal process, or governmental request, or when we believe disclosure is necessary to protect our rights, your safety, or the safety of others.
legal_privacy_body.s4_service_text: We use third-party services for email delivery, analytics, and infrastructure hosting. These providers are contractually obligated to protect your data and use it only for the purposes we specify.
legal_privacy_body.s5_p1_pre: We use cookies and similar technologies to maintain session state, remember your preferences, and understand how you use our platform. For full details on our cookie practices, see our
legal_privacy_body.s5_p2: We use essential cookies that are necessary for the platform to function (such as authentication tokens) and optional analytics cookies that help us understand usage patterns. You can control cookie preferences through your browser settings.

legal_privacy_body.s6_correction_text: Request correction of inaccurate or incomplete data

legal_privacy_body.s6_portability_text: Request your data in a structured, machine-readable format

legal_privacy_body.s6_outro_post: . We will respond to your request within 30 days.

legal_risk_body.callout: IMPORTANT: Please read this Risk Disclosure Statement carefully before using any BabahAlgo services. Trading in foreign exchange (forex), commodities, and financial derivatives involves substantial risk of loss and is not suitable for all investors.
legal_risk_body.s1_p1: Trading in foreign exchange, contracts for difference (CFDs), commodities, and other financial instruments carries a high level of risk. The high degree of leverage available in these markets can work against you as well as for you. Before deciding to trade, you should carefully consider your investment objectives, level of experience, and risk appetite. The possibility exists that you could sustain a loss of some or all of your initial investment, and therefore you should not invest money that you cannot afford to lose.
legal_risk_body.s2_p1: Leveraged trading means that both profits and losses are magnified. A relatively small market movement can have a proportionally larger impact on the funds you have deposited. This can work against you as well as for you. You may sustain a total loss of initial margin funds and any additional funds deposited with the broker to maintain your position. If the market moves against your position or margin levels are increased, you may be called upon to deposit additional funds on short notice to maintain your position. Failure to comply with a request for additional funds may result in your position being liquidated at a loss, and you will be liable for any resulting deficit.
legal_risk_body.s3_p1: Financial markets are subject to rapid and unpredictable price movements caused by economic events, geopolitical developments, central bank decisions, natural disasters, and other factors beyond anyone's control. Market gaps, sudden spikes in volatility, and liquidity disruptions can cause significant losses even when risk management measures are in place. Weekend gaps, holiday market closures, and unexpected news events can result in positions being closed at prices significantly different from the intended stop-loss levels.
legal_risk_body.s4_intro: BabahAlgo employs algorithmic trading strategies that are developed based on historical data and statistical models. These strategies are subject to the following specific risks:
legal_risk_body.s4_model_text: Trading models are based on historical patterns that may not repeat in the future. Market regime changes can cause models to underperform or generate losses.
legal_risk_body.s4_overfit_text: Despite rigorous validation procedures, there is a risk that strategies may be inadvertently fitted to historical noise rather than genuine market patterns.
legal_risk_body.s4_tech_text: Algorithmic trading depends on technology infrastructure including servers, network connections, and software. Hardware failures, software bugs, connectivity issues, and power outages can disrupt trading and cause losses.
legal_risk_body.s4_exec_text: The difference between expected and actual execution prices (slippage) can reduce returns. During periods of high volatility or low liquidity, slippage may be significant.
legal_risk_body.s5_p1: Past performance is not indicative of future results. Historical returns, backtested results, and simulated performance do not guarantee future profitability. Performance data shown on our platform represents the results of a specific account or strategy configuration and may not be representative of all client experiences. Actual client returns may differ based on account size, timing of entry, fee structure, broker execution quality, and other factors.
legal_risk_body.s6_p1: Client funds held at brokers are subject to the financial stability and regulatory compliance of those brokers. While we work exclusively with regulated brokers that maintain segregated client accounts, there remains a risk of broker insolvency, regulatory action, or operational failure that could affect the availability or safety of your funds. BabahAlgo does not guarantee the solvency or performance of any broker partner.
legal_risk_body.s7_p1: Under certain market conditions, it may be difficult or impossible to liquidate a position at the desired price. This can occur during major news events, market opens following weekends or holidays, or during periods of extreme market stress. In such conditions, stop-loss orders may be executed at prices significantly worse than the specified level, resulting in larger-than-expected losses.
legal_risk_body.s8_p1: Changes in laws, regulations, or regulatory interpretation in any jurisdiction where BabahAlgo operates or where clients reside may affect the availability, legality, or terms of our services. Tax treatment of trading profits and losses varies by jurisdiction and may change. You are responsible for understanding and complying with the tax and regulatory requirements applicable to your situation.

For Robot Crypto subscribers, you hold the Binance API key (Read + Trade permissions only, never Withdraw) and trades execute in your own Binance Futures account. Our fee structure is flat monthly subscription — no profit share, no performance fee. We do NOT offer PAMM or managed-account products in any form.
legal_risk_body.s10_p1: By using BabahAlgo services, you acknowledge that you have read and understood this Risk Disclosure Statement. You confirm that you understand the risks involved in trading financial instruments and that you are willing to accept these risks. You acknowledge that BabahAlgo has not made any guarantees regarding the performance of its trading strategies or the safety of your investment.
legal_risk_body.s10_p2: If you do not understand any aspect of this Risk Disclosure Statement, you should seek independent financial advice before using our services.

legal_regulatory_body.s1_p1: BabahAlgo is operated by CV Babah Digital, a commercial partnership registered under Indonesian law. BabahAlgo operates as a technology provider and trading infrastructure service, not as a regulated financial institution, broker, or investment advisor.

Our role is limited to providing technology services and trading infrastructure. Clients who are Indonesian residents should ensure they trade through BAPPEBTI-regulated brokers and comply with all applicable Indonesian regulations regarding futures and derivatives trading.
legal_regulatory_body.s2_p3: We monitor BAPPEBTI regulations and guidance on digital asset trading, commodity futures, and financial technology services to ensure our service structure remains compliant with the evolving regulatory framework in Indonesia.
